entries.name: Fake KYC Update / Account Block Threat
entries.how_it_works: A message impersonating a bank, wallet, or mobile operator claims the recipient's KYC (Know Your Customer) details have expired or are incomplete, and that the account, SIM, or wallet will be blocked or deactivated within hours unless it is 're-verified' immediately. The message pushes the recipient to click a link to a look-alike site, call a number, or reply with personal/bank details, and the urgency is designed to prevent the recipient from checking with the real institution first.
typical_phrases: your kyc is not updated, account will be suspended today
update your kyc within 2 hours to avoid deactivation
your sim card kyc pending, click link to update now
dear customer your account will be blocked, complete kyc verification
red_flags: Threat of an account/SIM/wallet being blocked within a very short deadline
Link goes to a domain that only resembles the real bank/operator, not its actual website
Asks for KYC documents, PAN, Aadhaar, or OTP over SMS/WhatsApp instead of the bank's app or branch
Message arrives from an unknown number, not the bank's official short code
entries.what_to_do: Do not click the link or share any document, PIN, or OTP. Open the bank or operator's official app or website directly (never through the message's link) to check your real KYC status, or call the number printed on your card/bill.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, based on general public awareness of KYC-update phishing scams reported by RBI and telecom operators in India; no text copied from any specific message, article, or dataset in this repo.

entries.name: Fake Electricity Bill Disconnection Threat
entries.how_it_works: The message poses as the local electricity board and warns that the recipient's power connection will be disconnected tonight because of an unpaid or 'not updated' bill. It asks the recipient to call a given mobile number or install a remote-access app (often disguised as an 'update' app) to speak to a 'customer care executive' who will supposedly help pay the bill electronically, and that app or call is used to steal payment credentials.
typical_phrases: your electricity will be disconnected tonight, previous bill not updated
power cut scheduled due to unpaid bill, contact executive immediately
download this app to pay your electricity bill and avoid disconnection
dear consumer your connection will be cut at 9:30pm today
red_flags: Disconnection threatened within a few hours, with no prior official notice
Asks to call a personal mobile number instead of the board's listed helpline
Pushes installation of a screen-sharing or 'quick support' app
Bill amount or consumer number is vague or not mentioned at all
entries.what_to_do: Never install a remote-access app because of an SMS. Check your bill status only on your electricity board's official website/app or its published helpline number, and pay only through that channel.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, based on widely reported 'fake power bill disconnection' scams covered by Indian police cybercrime advisories; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Fake Courier / Customs Fee Demand
entries.how_it_works: A message claims a parcel addressed to the recipient (often from abroad, or from a well-known courier) is held at customs or a courier facility because a small customs duty, handling fee, or 'clearance charge' is unpaid. It asks the recipient to pay a small amount through a link or UPI ID to release the parcel; the payment page is designed to also capture card/UPI credentials for larger theft, or the parcel does not exist at all.
typical_phrases: your parcel is held at customs, pay rs 350 clearance fee to release
courier could not deliver, pending customs duty payment required
pay a small handling charge to receive your international package
action required: your shipment is on hold at the airport, settle dues now
red_flags: Recipient was not expecting any parcel, or does not recognise the courier
Very small 'fee' relative to a supposedly valuable/international parcel
Payment link/UPI is not the courier company's known official channel
No tracking number, or a tracking number that cannot be verified on the courier's real website
entries.what_to_do: Do not pay through the link. Check the shipment status only on the courier's official app/website with a tracking number you recognise, and contact the courier through their listed customer-care channel, not the number in the message.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, based on general public awareness of courier/customs-fee phishing scams reported by Indian consumer and cybercrime advisories; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Fake 'Parcel Address Mismatch' Verification
entries.how_it_works: A message claims a delivery attempt failed because the recipient's address is incomplete or doesn't match records, and asks them to click a link to 're-confirm' or 'update' their address and sometimes payment details before the parcel is returned to sender. The link leads to a fake delivery-tracking page that harvests personal and card details rather than actually rescheduling any delivery.
typical_phrases: we could not deliver your parcel, address mismatch, confirm details here
your package is on hold, update your delivery address within 24 hours
delivery failed due to incomplete address, click to reschedule
your order will be returned unless you verify your shipping address now
red_flags: Recipient is not currently expecting any delivery
Link uses a domain that is not the courier or e-commerce site's real domain
Asks for card or bank details to 'confirm' an address, which real couriers never require
Generic greeting with no real order number or tracking ID
entries.what_to_do: Ignore the link. Check any pending orders directly in the shopping app or the courier's official tracking page using a tracking number you already have.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, based on general public reporting on fake delivery/address-verification phishing; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Fake Lottery / KBC-style Prize Win
entries.how_it_works: The recipient is told they have won a large cash prize, lottery, or a TV-show-style jackpot (sometimes name-dropping a real quiz show) that they never entered. To claim it, they are asked to pay a 'processing fee', 'tax', or 'release charge' in advance, or to share bank details for the prize to be 'transferred'. No prize ever arrives; the up-front payment is the actual goal.
typical_phrases: congratulations you have won 25 lakh in the lucky draw, pay processing fee to claim
your number has been selected for the kbc lucky winner prize, contact our manager
you are a winner of our anniversary lottery, share your bank details to receive the amount
claim your prize of rs 10,00,000 by paying a small registration fee today
red_flags: You never entered any such lottery, draw, or contest
Any request to pay money before receiving a prize
Urgency to respond within hours or the prize is 'forfeited'
Contact only through WhatsApp/personal mobile number, not an official company channel
entries.what_to_do: Do not pay anything or share bank details. Legitimate prizes never require an upfront fee to be released; ignore or block the sender and report it if it references a real brand or show.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, based on general public awareness of lottery and 'KBC lucky winner' scams widely reported in India; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Part-Time 'Like & Earn' Task Job Scam
entries.how_it_works: A message or Telegram/WhatsApp invite offers easy part-time income for simple tasks like liking YouTube videos, rating apps, or joining a channel, paying a small real amount for the first task or two to build trust. Once the recipient is engaged, they are moved into a 'task group' where larger 'investment' deposits are required to unlock bigger payouts, and withdrawals are blocked until yet more deposits are made - the deposited money is never returned.
typical_phrases: earn 500 rupees daily by liking youtube videos, part time work from home
join our telegram channel for simple online tasks and daily payment
no investment required initially, just complete tasks and get paid instantly
recharge your task wallet to unlock the next higher paying task
red_flags: Recruitment happens on WhatsApp/Telegram, not a real company's HR channel
Small genuine-looking payouts at first, followed by requests to deposit money
Withdrawals are blocked until you 'top up' your task wallet again
No formal offer letter, interview, or verifiable company details
entries.what_to_do: Never deposit money to 'unlock' earnings from a task-based job. Stop responding once you're asked to pay anything, and do not share bank/UPI credentials with the group.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, based on general public awareness of task-based/part-time job scams on Telegram and WhatsApp widely reported in Indian media; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Fake Instant Loan Offer / Processing Fee Scam
entries.how_it_works: The message offers an instant, pre-approved personal loan at an unusually low interest rate with minimal documentation, targeting people who may be in financial need. After the recipient shows interest, they are asked to pay a 'processing fee', 'GST', or 'insurance charge' upfront via UPI to release the loan amount; the loan is never disbursed, and sometimes the app itself is used to harvest contacts and photos for later harassment.
typical_phrases: you are pre-approved for a rs 2 lakh instant loan, no documents required
get a personal loan in 10 minutes, just pay a small processing fee first
your loan is approved, transfer the gst amount to receive the disbursed amount
install our loan app to get instant cash, apply now with just your phone number
red_flags: Loan approval before any real credit check or documentation
Any fee, deposit, or 'insurance' required before the loan amount is disbursed
Pressure to install an unfamiliar lending app with broad phone permissions
No RBI registration or NBFC name that can be verified
entries.what_to_do: Never pay a fee to receive a loan; legitimate lenders deduct fees from the disbursed amount, not before it. Verify any lending app or NBFC on the RBI's list of registered entities before installing anything.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, based on RBI public advisories about unauthorised digital lending apps and loan-processing-fee scams; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Fake Bank Call/SMS Asking to Share OTP
entries.how_it_works: Someone impersonating a bank employee calls the recipient (or sends an SMS) about a supposed problem - a blocked card, a failed transaction, a reward point expiry - and asks the recipient to read out or forward the OTP they are about to receive, or to enter it on a page/app the caller directs them to. The OTP is then used to authorise a real transaction on the victim's account, draining funds while the victim believes they are just 'verifying' something.
typical_phrases: this is your bank calling, please share the otp to verify your card
for security purpose kindly tell me the 6 digit code you just received
to reverse this wrong transaction please forward the otp sms to us
your reward points will expire, share the otp to redeem them now
red_flags: Any request, by call or SMS, to share, read out, or forward an OTP
Caller creates urgency around a problem you did not report yourself
Caller already knows some of your details, making the call sound legitimate
Bank/UPI apps and staff never need your OTP - the OTP is only for you
entries.what_to_do: Never share an OTP with anyone, no matter who they claim to be. Hang up and call your bank back using the number on your card or their official app/website if you're unsure.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, based on RBI and bank public awareness campaigns that repeatedly warn 'do not share your OTP with anyone'; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Fake UPI 'Collect Request' / Refund Scam
entries.how_it_works: The scammer, often posing as a buyer on an online marketplace or a helpful 'customer care' agent processing a refund, sends the victim a UPI collect (payment request) notification and tells them to just 'enter your UPI PIN to receive the money'. In UPI, entering the PIN on a collect request actually authorises a payment OUT of the victim's account, not in - so the victim ends up sending money while believing they are receiving it.
typical_phrases: i've sent you the payment request, just enter your upi pin to accept and receive the amount
to get your refund approved, accept the request and enter your pin
sir i am interested in your item, accept my payment request to get the money
customer care here, enter upi pin on the collect request to process your refund
red_flags: Being told to enter a UPI PIN in order to 'receive' money
A refund or payment being processed through a 'collect request' rather than the sender simply paying you
Pressure from an unknown buyer/agent to act quickly on a payment request
The counterpart avoids voice calls or video verification
entries.what_to_do: Never enter your UPI PIN to receive money - a PIN is only ever needed to send/pay. Decline unexpected collect requests and verify refunds directly in the app or with the seller through the platform's official channel.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, based on public awareness campaigns by NPCI/banks explaining that a UPI PIN is only needed to pay, never to receive; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Sextortion via Video Call Screenshot Threat
entries.how_it_works: A stranger (often posing as an attractive woman) initiates a video call, sometimes on WhatsApp, that turns out to show explicit content; the attacker secretly screen-records the victim's own video feed too, sometimes after tricking them into undressing. Immediately after, the attacker sends a screenshot and threatens to share it with the victim's contacts, family, or on social media unless money is paid quickly, often repeatedly.
typical_phrases: i have recorded your video call, pay now or i will send it to all your contacts
your family will see this video if you don't pay within 30 minutes
send the payment immediately or this gets uploaded to social media
i have your number's contact list, one payment and i delete everything
red_flags: Unknown caller escalating quickly to video/explicit content
Screenshot or recording is presented immediately after the call as leverage
Extremely short deadline paired with a threat to contact family/friends
Repeated demands for more money even after paying once
entries.what_to_do: Stop all contact and do not pay - payment rarely stops further demands. Block the number, do not delete the evidence, and report to the Indian Cyber Crime portal (cybercrime.gov.in) or the 1930 helpline.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, based on public awareness advisories from Indian police cybercrime cells about video-call sextortion; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: 'Digital Arrest' Fake Law-Enforcement Video Call
entries.how_it_works: A caller claiming to be from the police, CBI, customs, or a courier-linked cybercrime cell tells the victim that a parcel/SIM/bank account in their name is linked to a crime (drugs, money laundering) and that they are under 'digital arrest' - required to stay on a video call, sometimes in front of a fake uniformed 'officer' on screen, and not tell anyone, while being pressured to transfer money to a 'safe government account' to prove innocence or avoid real arrest.
typical_phrases: you are under digital arrest, do not disconnect this call or leave your house
your aadhaar is linked to an illegal parcel, cbi is investigating your case
transfer funds to this rbi verification account to clear your name
this call is being monitored by law, do not tell any family member
red_flags: No real law-enforcement process is conducted entirely over a video call
Instruction to stay on the call continuously and not contact anyone else
Any request to transfer money to 'verify' innocence or avoid arrest
Fake uniforms, background, or official-looking documents shown on screen
entries.what_to_do: Hang up - there is no such thing as a 'digital arrest'. Verify independently by visiting a local police station or calling the cybercrime helpline 1930; never transfer money during or after such a call.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, based on 2024-2025 Indian government and police public awareness campaigns explicitly stating there is no provision for 'digital arrest'; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Fake Investment / Stock-Tips Group Scam
entries.how_it_works: Victims are added to a WhatsApp or Telegram 'investment community' run by someone posing as a SEBI-registered advisor or successful trader, who shares a few genuinely correct tips to build credibility, then pushes the group toward a trading app or portal where deposited funds show fabricated, fast-growing 'profits' on screen. When the victim tries to withdraw, the platform demands more fees/taxes, or simply stops responding, and the deposited money and shown profits are both fictitious.
typical_phrases: join our exclusive stock trading group, guaranteed daily returns
our sebi registered expert gives 100% accurate intraday calls
your portfolio has grown to 5 lakhs, pay a small tax to withdraw your profit
limited seats available, deposit now to start earning from tomorrow
red_flags: Guaranteed or 'sure-shot' returns - no legitimate investment can promise this
Trading happens through an unfamiliar app/website, not a SEBI-registered broker
Any fee, tax, or 'unlock charge' demanded before a withdrawal is allowed
Screenshots of huge, fast profits used to pressure larger deposits
entries.what_to_do: Only invest through SEBI-registered brokers and platforms you can verify independently. Treat any group promising guaranteed returns as a scam, and never pay extra fees to 'unlock' a withdrawal.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, based on SEBI public investor-awareness advisories about fraudulent trading tips and fake portfolio apps; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Fake Customer Care Number (Search-Engine / Social Media)
entries.how_it_works: The victim, trying to resolve a genuine issue (a bank complaint, a food-delivery refund, a wallet problem), searches online or calls a number found on social media claiming to be a brand's customer care. The number is actually run by a scammer who, under the guise of 'resolving' the issue, asks the victim to share OTPs, install a remote-access app, or make a small 'refund verification' payment - and uses that access to steal money instead of helping.
typical_phrases: thank you for calling customer care, please share the otp to verify your complaint
to process your refund, kindly download this remote support app
for verification purpose send rs 1 to this upi id, it will be refunded with your amount
your complaint is registered, our executive will guide you to fix it, please stay on call and follow the steps
red_flags: Number was found through a general web/social-media search, not the brand's official app or website
Being asked to install a remote-access/screen-share app to 'help' with a complaint
Any request to pay even a small amount to 'verify' or 'unlock' a refund
Executive asks for OTP or full card details to 'process' a complaint
entries.what_to_do: Only use customer-care numbers listed inside the official app or on the brand's verified website. Never install remote-access apps or share OTPs with anyone claiming to help you over the phone.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, based on widely reported 'fake customer care number' scams covered by Indian consumer-protection and cybercrime advisories; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Premium-Rate Prize Call-Back Lure
entries.how_it_works: A message claims the recipient has won a cash prize, holiday, or gadget from a supposed draw or a well-known brand's promotion they never entered, and asks them to call a number to 'claim' it. The number is a premium-rate line that charges a high per-minute cost, and the call is deliberately kept going (holding music, transfers, T&Cs) so the victim runs up a large phone bill; sometimes the 'claim' also asks for a small delivery/tax payment on top.
typical_phrases: you have won a guaranteed cash prize, call this number now to claim
your mobile number has been selected for a free holiday, ring to collect
urgent! this is our final attempt to contact you about your prize, call now
congratulations, claim your award by calling our claims line before it expires
red_flags: You never entered the competition or draw referenced
The claim number is a normal-looking mobile/landline number with no brand association
Message pressures an urgent callback ('final attempt', 'expires today')
Prize is vague ('a prize', 'cash or holiday') rather than something specific and verifiable
entries.what_to_do: Do not call the number. If a promotion is genuine, you can verify it independently through the brand's official customer-care channel without using the number given in the message.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, based on general public awareness of classic premium-rate-line 'prize claim' SMS scams (widely documented internationally, e.g. UK Ofcom/consumer advisories); no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Genuine Bank/App OTP Delivery Alert
entries.how_it_works: A bank, wallet, or app sends a one-time password for a transaction or login the recipient themselves just initiated, along with a short reminder never to share it with anyone. The message is purely informational: it delivers a code and a warning, and never asks the recipient to click a link, call a number, or forward/read out the code to anyone.
typical_phrases: your otp for the transaction is 483920, valid for 10 minutes, do not share with anyone
use 719045 to complete your login, this code is confidential
otp for your payment is 205817, bank staff will never ask for this
your one time password is 664210, please do not share it even with bank representatives
red_flags: Message is purely informational and does not ask you to do anything with the code
Explicitly warns not to share the OTP, including with bank staff
Arrives right after you yourself requested a login/transaction
Comes from the bank/app's known official sender ID, not a personal number
entries.what_to_do: No action needed beyond using the OTP yourself for the transaction you started. If you did not request any transaction, treat an unexpected OTP as a warning sign and check your account/app directly.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, describing the standard, harmless form of a genuine bank/app OTP message; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Genuine Utility/Telecom Bill Reminder
entries.how_it_works: A telecom operator, electricity board, or other utility sends a routine reminder that a bill is due or overdue, usually stating the amount and due date, and pointing to the provider's own app, website, or standard payment options - without threats of same-day disconnection or requests to install unfamiliar apps or share OTPs.
typical_phrases: your electricity bill of rs 1240 for this month is due on the 15th, pay via our app or website
your postpaid bill of rs 599 is due, kindly pay before the due date to avoid late fee
dear customer your monthly bill has been generated, view and pay in myaccount app
reminder: your broadband bill is due in 3 days, pay online to avoid service interruption
red_flags: States a specific, plausible amount and due date rather than vague urgency
Points to the provider's own named app/website, not a personal number or unrelated link
No threat of disconnection within hours, and no request to install a remote-access app
Consistent with your existing service/account with that provider
entries.what_to_do: Pay through the provider's official app, website, or usual payment method. If anything feels off (unfamiliar amount, unusually urgent tone), check your account directly instead of using any link in the message.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, describing the standard, harmless form of a routine utility/telecom bill reminder; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Genuine Courier/E-commerce Delivery Update
entries.how_it_works: A courier or e-commerce platform sends a routine update about a real order the recipient placed - out for delivery, delivered, or a delay notice - typically including an order or tracking number, and directing the recipient to the shopping app or courier's own tracking page for details, without demanding any payment to release the parcel.
typical_phrases: your order #48213 is out for delivery today between 2pm-6pm
your package has been delivered, thank you for shopping with us
shipment update: your order is delayed by one day due to weather, new eta tomorrow
track your parcel anytime in the app using order id 48213
red_flags: References an order/tracking number you can recognise and independently check
Matches a purchase you actually made recently
No request for a customs, clearance, or 'address verification' payment
Link, if present, points to the courier's or platform's own known tracking domain
entries.what_to_do: No payment or link-click is needed to receive a routine delivery. If in doubt, check the order status directly in the shopping app rather than through the message's link.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, describing the standard, harmless form of a genuine delivery status update; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Legitimate Commercial Promotion from a Named Brand
entries.how_it_works: An identifiable, real business (a telecom operator, retailer, bank, or app) sends a promotional message about a genuine sale, cashback, recharge offer, or subscription benefit. It may be pushy or unsolicited, but the offer, brand, and terms are real and verifiable, there's no deception about who is sending it or what is being offered, and it does not demand upfront payment of a 'fee' to release money or a prize.
typical_phrases: flat 30% off this weekend only at our store, shop now
recharge with our 299 plan and get 10gb extra data free
get 5% cashback on your next purchase using our app
your favourite show's new season is now streaming, watch on our app
red_flags: Sent by a brand/operator you actually have an account or relationship with
Offer terms are specific and consistent with things that brand normally sells
No claim of a 'prize' you did nothing to earn, and no upfront fee to receive anything
Link, if present, goes to the brand's own known app/website domain
entries.what_to_do: Treat as ordinary marketing - engage with the offer only through the brand's official app/website if interested, and reply STOP/unsubscribe if unwanted; no urgent action or verification is required.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, describing the standard, harmless form of a real brand's promotional message, consistent with the 'promo' category defined in docs/label_rubric.md; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Genuine Password/PIN Reset Notification
entries.how_it_works: A service sends a short notice confirming that a password, PIN, or security setting was just changed - either as a code to complete a reset the user is actively doing, or as an after-the-fact confirmation - along with guidance to contact support if the user did not make this change themselves. It does not ask the recipient to click a link to 'undo' the change or to share any credentials.
typical_phrases: your password was successfully changed just now, if this wasn't you contact support
use code 552019 to reset your account password, valid for 15 minutes
your account pin has been updated, if you did not request this please reach out to us
security alert: your login password was changed from a new device
red_flags: Confirms an action rather than demanding one, or gives a code only for a reset you started
Points to official support channels rather than an embedded 'reverse this' link
Matches something you actually just did (changing your password)
No request to share the new password or any OTP with the sender
entries.what_to_do: If you made the change, no action is needed. If you did not, contact the service through its official app/website immediately to secure your account - never through a link in the alert itself.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, describing the standard, harmless form of a password/PIN change notification; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Genuine Appointment/Interview Reminder
entries.how_it_works: A clinic, office, or recruiter sends a plain reminder about a scheduled appointment or interview the recipient already arranged, stating the date, time, and location or a call link, without financial requests or urgent threats.
typical_phrases: this is a reminder for your appointment tomorrow at 10am at our clinic
your interview is scheduled for friday 3pm, please join the link 5 minutes early
reminder: your consultation with dr sharma is confirmed for today evening
your meeting with the hr team is rescheduled to monday 11am, please confirm availability
red_flags: Matches an appointment/interview the recipient actually arranged
No request for payment, OTP, or personal financial details
Comes from, or references, a specific known person/organisation
Tone is informational, not urgent or threatening
entries.what_to_do: Simply attend as scheduled, or contact the sender through a known number/email if you need to reschedule; no security action is required.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, describing an ordinary, harmless appointment/interview reminder message; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Genuine Subscription Renewal / Recharge Notice
entries.how_it_works: A streaming, mobile, or app subscription service informs the recipient that their existing paid subscription or recharge is due for renewal soon, at the price they already agreed to, with the option to manage or cancel it in the app - not a fresh 'offer' asking for new payment details by link.
typical_phrases: your monthly subscription renews on the 5th for rs 199, manage anytime in the app
your data pack expires tomorrow, recharge from the app to continue uninterrupted service
your premium membership auto-renews in 3 days at the current rate
reminder: your yearly plan will renew soon, no action needed unless you wish to cancel
red_flags: References a subscription/plan you actually have
Amount matches the price you already agreed to, not a surprise charge
Managed entirely within the official app, not through an external payment link
No threat of immediate service loss within hours
entries.what_to_do: No action is required unless you want to change or cancel the plan - do that directly inside the official app, not via any link in the message.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, describing the standard, harmless form of a subscription/recharge renewal reminder; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Genuine Bank Statement / Transaction Alert
entries.how_it_works: A bank sends a routine debit/credit alert or e-statement notification for a transaction the account holder actually made, stating the amount, a masked account/card number, and available balance, purely for the customer's own record - with no request to click a link or share any credential.
typical_phrases: rs 1500 debited from your account ending 4821 on 03-oct, available balance rs 23,400
your salary of rs 45000 has been credited to your account ending 1122
your monthly e-statement is now available, view it in netbanking or the app
a payment of rs 799 was made using your card ending 5567 at a merchant
red_flags: Matches a transaction the recipient actually recognises making
No link asking to 'verify' or 'reverse' the transaction
Only a masked account/card number is shown, never the full number
Purely informational tone with no request for action
entries.what_to_do: No action needed if the transaction is recognised. If it is not, contact the bank directly through its official app or the number on the back of your card - never through a link in the alert.
entries.source_notes: Original text written for this project, describing the standard, harmless form of a bank debit/credit alert; no text copied from any specific message or article.

entries.name: Genuine E-commerce Order Confirmation
entries.how_it_works: An online shopping platform confirms that an order the recipient placed has been received, billed, or invoiced, including an order number and amount that matches what the recipient actually paid, with an option to view the invoice or track the order in the app - no request to 'update' payment details or click an unfamiliar link to release the order.
typical_phrases: your order for rs 899 has been placed successfully, order id 77341
thank you for shopping with us, view your e-invoice in the app
your order has been packed and will be shipped within 24 hours
payment of rs 1299 received for order #90231, track it anytime in the app
red_flags: Matches a purchase the recipient actually made, with a recognisable amount
Order/invoice details are viewable directly inside the shopping app
No request for additional payment or card details to 'confirm' the order
Tone is a simple confirmation, not urgent or threatening
entries.what_to_do: No action needed - you can view the order/invoice directly in the app at any time. Treat any message asking for extra payment on an already-placed order with suspicion.

entries.name: Genuine Government Scheme / Service Update
entries.how_it_works: A government department or scheme (e.g. a subsidy, ration, vaccination, or civic-services update) sends an informational message about eligibility, status, or a scheduled camp/appointment, directing the recipient to the department's official portal or office for any action, rather than asking for payment or personal documents to be sent back over SMS/WhatsApp.
typical_phrases: your subsidy application status has been updated, check on the official portal
vaccination slots now available near you, book on the official app
your ration card details are due for renewal, visit your nearest centre with documents
your application reference number 88214 has been received and is under process
red_flags: Directs you to the government department's own portal/office rather than a private link
No request to pay a 'fee' to receive a benefit you're entitled to
No request to send documents or OTPs back over SMS/WhatsApp
Matches a scheme or application you actually engaged with
entries.what_to_do: Handle any action through the official government portal or in person at the relevant office; never pay a 'fee' or share documents through a link in the message.

entries.name: Genuine Recruiter Outreach / Job Offer
entries.how_it_works: A recruiter or HR contact from an identifiable company reaches out about a real job opening or interview, referencing the role, company name, and next steps (interview, documents to bring), without demanding any payment, security deposit, or 'registration fee' from the candidate at any stage.
typical_phrases: we reviewed your profile for the software engineer role at our company, are you available for an interview this week
congratulations, we would like to move forward with your application, please share your availability
your interview for the marketing associate position is confirmed for tuesday
please bring your original documents for verification at the time of joining
red_flags: Names a specific, identifiable company and role
No request for money, security deposit, or 'training fee' at any stage
Contact matches a job application the recipient actually made
Process follows normal steps: interview, offer, then joining - not payment first
entries.what_to_do: Verify the company and role independently (official website, LinkedIn) before sharing documents, and never pay any fee to a recruiter for a job opportunity.
